reasons.correctness: SupportTicketCreatedEventListener uses plain @EventListener. Spring runs it synchronously inside createTicket's transaction, so the mail is still sent before commit and on rollback. The core task is unfixed; hidden tests pass because they call the listener directly.
reasons.convention_fit: Breaks the side-effect convention: @EventListener instead of @TransactionalEventListener(phase = TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT). Followed: constructor injection via @RequiredArgsConstructor, feature package support/ticket/event, catch-and-log in the listener.
reasons.design_fit: The event and listener split is sound and lives in the ticket feature. Without AFTER_COMMIT the side effect still runs inside the transaction, so the added indirection delivers none of the intended decoupling.
reasons.test_quality: SupportTicketCreatedEventListenerUnitTest covers delegation and the swallowed failure with MockitoExtension. No test checks that createTicket publishes the event and no longer calls EmailService. Nothing pins after-commit behaviour.
reasons.graph_use: One generic query (MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.file_path LIMIT 1) located nothing relevant. No existing listener was found or read; the agent read AccountActivatedEvent directly and edited without graph guidance.
